summary: Steel lookout in Sproul State Forest, Clinton County, in service from 1919 or 1920 by different accounts and rebuilt around 2018 to 2020; staffed in fire season.

facts.design: Aermotor tower (65 ft, 7 by 7 ft cab) later replaced by a modern galvanized steel structure

events.note: Register gives 1919 for service start. A 1926 account and the story map say 1920.
Listed on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register as the Tamarack Tower Site, a separate entry describing a bald tower used around 1917 that is no longer standing
Story map date for the replacement. The register says circa 2020.
Register says circa 2020, with a modern steel structure replacing the original tower

evidence.supports: in service since 1919; still staffed by PA Bureau of Forestry in fire season
evidence.quote: In service since 1919, the Tamarack Fire Lookout is still staffed by the Pennsylvania Bureau of Forestry in fire season.
It was a 65' Aermotor tower with a 7'x7' cab.

evidence.supports: circa 2020 replacement with a modern steel structure
evidence.quote: Circa 2020, the original tower was replaced with a modern steel structure.

evidence.supports: 2021 visit: modern galvanized steel tower in pristine condition
evidence.quote: Tower is a modern galvanized steel tower and is in pristine condition.
It is staffed during fire season.

evidence.supports: former tower site: bald tower used circa 1917, no longer standing
evidence.quote: This bald tower was used circa 1917 and is no longer standing.

evidence.supports: story map: built 1920, 60-foot tower replaced 2018, Clinton County, Sproul State Forest, 80 feet, staffed in wildfire season
evidence.quote: Built in 1920 by the Aermotor Windmill Company, the 60 foot tower was replaced in 2018. Located in Clinton County in Sproul State Forest. It has a height of 80 feet and is actively staffed during wildfire season.
Constructed in 1920, it is of regulation height and is located on Tamarack ridge at an elevation of about 2,200 feet.

evidence.supports: May 1920 Lock Haven Express: new steel fire tower nearly complete
evidence.quote: From the new steel fire tower at Tamarack, which is now about completed, a constant lookout is maintained for forest fires in Clinton county.

evidence.supports: Lock Haven Express item dated May 12, 1920
village of Tamarack a few miles north; the tower was named after it
evidence.quote: A few miles to the north lies the little village of Tamarack, from which the tower was named.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The former-site entry describes a bald tower used around 1917 that is no longer standing. The current register entry and the 2021 visit describe a standing lookout, so the former-site entry most likely refers to an earlier structure at this location, though the sources do not say so outright.

sources.title: Tamarack Tower Site
sources.publisher: Former Fire Lookout Sites Register, Forest Fire Lookout Association

notes_for_editor: Build year: register 1919; story map and 1926 account 1920; the May 1920 newspaper item calls the steel tower nearly complete, which fits both. The record keeps 1919. Replacement: register circa 2020, story map 2018; the record keeps 2018 and both are listed. The former-site entry (FFLOS US 503) may be an earlier tower; it is not clearly this structure. Staffing: the register says staffed in fire season, the 2021 visit says 'Staffed? Sometimes', and the story map says actively staffed in wildfire season. The register has the NHLR sign posted and directions signed, but no access level is recorded, so no access fact was written. Design: the record's Aermotor applies to the original tower; the current steel structure's maker is not stated. Web search found nothing on this tower's history beyond the sources listed.
